headline: High-risk pair: LightAgent’s broad egress and MCP/browser tooling can leak or misroute workflow data into Prefect orchestration, with default-path compliance and cascading-error concerns.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can ingest and emit MCP/stdin-stdout payloads and run browsers, so attacker-controlled content could reach its tool pipeline. Prefect is an orchestration layer that can consume workflow metadata, creating a plausible bridge if LightAgent outputs are passed into flows. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF LightAgent outputs are copied into Prefect flow inputs without sanitization
IF an MCP server or shared message channel is configured between the agents
mitigations: Add an explicit content-sanitization step before any LightAgent output reaches Prefect
Disable automatic ingestion of browser/MCP text into downstream prompts
Use a provenance tag and reject untrusted tool output
requires-engineering: add schema validation at the orchestration boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches user conversations, long-term memory, tool results, and secrets, and has broad network egress. Prefect touches workflow metadata and also has broad egress. If LightAgent artifacts are handed to Prefect for orchestration or logging, sensitive context can leave the original boundary. The pairwise leak path is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF LightAgent conversation or memory data is passed into Prefect task parameters or logs
IF Prefect sends workflow metadata to external services while carrying LightAgent-derived content
mitigations: Restrict Prefect inputs to redacted metadata only
Turn off verbose logging for LightAgent-derived tasks
Separate secrets-handling workflows from orchestration metadata
requires-engineering: enforce field-level data-loss prevention at the handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightAgent supports multiple instances and subprocesses, but Prefect is not marked as writable to shared state here and no shared mutable resource is documented. The main overlap is orchestration metadata, not a proven write-write conflict. Uncertainty is limited, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same filesystem directory or git repository
IF Prefect is extended with mutable shared-state plugins
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Avoid concurrent writes to the same repo or artifact store
Use file locks around shared outputs
requires-engineering: add a coordinator lock service

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can produce tool results, provenance metadata, and workflow state that Prefect may treat as orchestration inputs. If Prefect trusts those outputs without verification, a bad LightAgent result can cascade into downstream automation. Prefect is an orchestrator, so the blast radius can extend beyond one task even though no direct action-taking is documented.
conditions: IF Prefect uses LightAgent-produced workflow state as authoritative input
IF downstream Prefect tasks execute based on unverified LightAgent tool results
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification gate before execution
Require typed outputs from LightAgent and reject free-form text
Log and compare LightAgent claims against source data
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and rollback handling

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent explicitly handles secrets and user conversations, while Prefect is a workflow orchestrator with workflow metadata and broad egress. That creates a compliance mismatch risk if regulated or secret-bearing data is routed through Prefect logs or external services. Only LightAgent is directly cited for sensitive data handling because Prefect’s profile does not show regulated-data handling.
conditions: IF regulated or secret-bearing LightAgent data is routed through Prefect logs, retries, or external callbacks
IF retention policies differ between LightAgent memory and Prefect workflow records
mitigations: Exclude secrets from Prefect task arguments
Set short retention on workflow logs
Document a data-class mapping for each handoff
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls per data class
